newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss shares end nervous day easier, above lows.
newsitem.headline: Swiss shares end nervous day easier, above lows.

text.p: 1530 GMT - Swiss shares ended easier but above the day's lows, continuing a recent weaker bias.

Dealers said trade was extremely nervous and influenced to a large extent by derivatives transactions. Insecurity about the future development of U.S. interest rates was seen keeping some investors away from the market. "Now the market's eyes are on the U.S. treasury and on Wall Street," one trader noted.
* The blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) ended off 36.2 points, or 0.79 percent, at 4,520.3 points. The index briefly slipped below 4,500 to hit a day's low at 4,494.8.

* Dealers said SMI futures were temporarily under heavy pressure which in turn led down SMI heavyweights such as Roche, Novartis and UBS. However, Novartis recovered from the day's lows to end off one franc at 1,738. Dealers said 1996 results had come in as expected but added the increase of the dividend to 20 francs from 16.80 and a favourable outlook were good news.
* Roche ended down 210 francs to 11,980, falling below the psychologically important level of 12,000 francs. Ciba CIGZn.S suffered from foreign buy orders, giving up 1.75 francs to 118.50.
* Among industrials, ABB stocks were among the losers of the day. They fell 45 francs to 1,690.
* Sulzer, which today reported a favourable outlook for 1997, gave up 12 francs to 967.
* UBS bearers lost 17 francs to 1,290. CS Group was down 0.75 francs to 162.75 francs. Insurer Winterthur bucked the trend, adding two francs to 968.
* Trade on Swiss Options and Financial Futures Exchange (Soffex) continued to see big price swings.

"It was extremely volatile," one dealer said. Volume was high in SMI futures, where 11,993 contracts changed hands. Trade in options was described as illiquid despite high volume. Of the total of 169,498 options contracts traded, Novartis accounted for nearly 30,000 and UBS for almost 45,000.
